events.title: Birth of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi
events.description: Mohandas K. Gandhi was born in Porbandar, in present-day Gujarat, India. He became the foremost leader of the Indian independence movement against British colonial rule.
events.significance: Gandhi pioneered nonviolent civil disobedience (satyagraha), inspiring civil rights and freedom movements worldwide, including those led by Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela. His birthday is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti in India and as the International Day of Non-Violence globally.

events.title: Saladin Captures Jerusalem
events.description: After defeating the Crusaders at the Battle of Hattin in July 1187 and besieging the city, the Muslim leader Saladin accepted the surrender of Jerusalem, which had been under Crusader control since 1099.
events.significance: The recapture of Jerusalem reshaped the political landscape of the Near East and prompted the Third Crusade, led by Richard the Lionheart, Philip II of France, and Frederick Barbarossa.

events.title: End of the Warsaw Uprising
events.description: After 63 days of fighting, Polish Home Army forces surrendered to German troops, ending the Warsaw Uprising. The revolt aimed to liberate the city from Nazi occupation ahead of the advancing Soviet Red Army.
events.significance: The uprising resulted in the deaths of roughly 150,000-200,000 Polish civilians and the near-total destruction of Warsaw. It remains a powerful symbol of Polish resistance and the tragic cost of World War II.

events.title: Peanuts Comic Strip Debuts
events.description: Charles M. Schulz's comic strip Peanuts made its first appearance in seven American newspapers, introducing Charlie Brown, Snoopy, and their friends.
events.significance: Peanuts became one of the most popular and influential comic strips in history, running nearly 50 years with 17,897 strips and shaping global popular culture, animation, and merchandising.

events.title: Death of Rock Hudson and Rise in AIDS Awareness
events.description: Actor Rock Hudson, a Hollywood leading man, died of AIDS-related illness at age 59, after publicly disclosing his diagnosis in July 1985.
events.significance: Hudson's disclosure and death brought unprecedented public attention to the AIDS epidemic, increasing awareness, boosting research funding, and shifting public and political discussion of the disease in the United States.
